axes.model_access:
**You pick the provider. The official lists 30+, primarily BYOK (bring your own API key).**

The official Model Selection Guide's provider table lists:

- **Cline** — no API key needed, just log in
- **OpenRouter** / **Anthropic** / **OpenAI**
- **OpenAI Codex** — use your ChatGPT subscription directly, no API key
- **Google Gemini** / **DeepSeek** / **Alibaba Qwen** / **Moonshot** / **Cerebras**
- **AWS Bedrock**
- **Ollama** — local models

The official also has an "all 30+ supported providers" page, additionally covering xAI Grok, Mistral, Groq,
Together, Hugging Face, Baseten, SambaNova, Nebius etc.

Two hookup paths:

- CLI command — `cline auth --provider anthropic --apikey sk-... --modelid ...`
- the official SDK supports OpenAI-compatible endpoints —
  `providerId: "openai-compatible"` + `baseUrl` + `apiKey`

⚠ **After switching providers, the quality of tool calling and structured output: the official gives no comparison.**
axes.runtime:
**This is the only subject on this site covering all three forms.**

| Form | How it runs |
|---|---|
| **CLI** | `npm i -g cline`; interactive and fully headless modes, headless for CI/CD and scripts; `--workspace /path/to/repo` sets the directory |
| **Desktop App** | native macOS and Windows apps; run agent sessions in any folder; scheduled tasks supported |
| **VS Code extension** | plus a JetBrains plugin |

`.clinerules` is **read jointly by the CLI / VS Code extension / JetBrains plugin**.
The three forms share the same open-source core.
axes.local_files:
**Two features: coordinated changes across the project, and rollbackable checkpoints.**

The README's **"Edits Code Across Your Project"** means: read the project structure, understand relationships between files,
then make coordinated changes across the codebase.

**While editing it watches linter and compiler errors**, proactively fixing missing imports,
type mismatches and syntax errors — the things that "go wrong without the user ever seeing them".

- In VS Code and JetBrains, **every edit is presented as a diff** — reviewable, modifiable, rollbackable
- all changes carry checkpoint records and can be undone wholesale
- the official Checkpoints page explains it tracks changes with a **shadow Git repository**,
  **not interfering with your main Git workflow**, creating a checkpoint after each tool call

**Read scope has two tiers**: by default "Read project files" (inside the workspace);
"Read all files" (outside the workspace) only takes effect after enabling a base toggle first.
Project-level ignores are controlled by `.clineignore` (the official also shows a hook-enforced approach).

⚠ **It has no "full semantic index" stage.** The built-in `search` tool is a
"Ripgrep-powered codebase search"; the official advice for large repos is
"use search instead of reading many files", and to break tasks down smaller.
(checked the Tools page and the Context Window Guide.)

**The official large-repo advice**: Use search instead of reading many files
axes.background:
**Long-running processes and scheduled tasks are both supported.**

Commands execute directly in the terminal with output visible in real time — installing packages, running builds, running tests, deploying, managing databases. For long-running processes like dev servers, **Cline keeps working in the background and reacts to new output**:
compile errors, test failures and service crashes are caught as they happen.

**The Desktop App form additionally has scheduled tasks (schedule routines)**:

- cron scheduling for periodic automation
- examples: daily PR summaries, weekly dependency checks, codebase health reports
- **schedules persist across restarts and run independently of any terminal session**

The CLI's headless mode targets CI/CD.
axes.tools:
**The built-in tool list has been verified** (official Tools reference, ClineCore runtime):

- `bash` — execute commands
- `editor` — view/edit files
- `read_files` — batch reads
- `apply_patch` — unified-diff patching
- `search` — ripgrep code search
- `fetch_web` — HTTP + HTML-to-markdown
- `ask_question` — ask the user

**MCP is its core extension surface.** The official has an **MCP Marketplace**;
the config file is `.cline/mcp.json`:

- tools are called via `use_mcp_tool`, resources accessed via `access_mcp_resource`
- transports support **stdio and HTTP**
- "MCP Rules" in `.clinerules` can group dispatch by trigger words

Other extension mechanisms: **Hooks** (PreToolUse / PostToolUse) · Skills · Workflows ·
plugins (custom tools registerable, currently limited to SDK / CLI / Kanban).

**The official statement about the MCP Marketplace**: one-click installation experience for hundreds of MCP servers
axes.context:
**The project-level rules file is `.clinerules`.**

It defines project-specific rules: coding standards, architecture conventions, deployment flows, testing requirements.
**Rules are read automatically by the CLI, VS Code extension and JetBrains plugin.**
Skills can additionally let the model load specific rules on demand.

The Desktop form mentions **"run agent sessions in any folder"**, i.e. cross-folder session management.

**The context mechanism has been verified**: near the limit, **Auto Compact summarizes automatically**.
Window size **is decided by the chosen model** — the official lists Claude Sonnet 4.5 at 1M,
GPT-5 at 400K, Gemini 2.5 Pro at 1M+.

**Cross-session memory runs on the Memory Bank**: a set of structured markdown files
(`projectbrief.md` / `productContext.md` / `activeContext.md` / `progress.md` etc.)
kept in the repo, with reads/writes driven by `.clinerules` instructions.

The official also has Focus Chain (todo injection) and `/newtask`, `/smol` for context handoff.

**The official wording on Auto Compact**: Creates a comprehensive summary...
Replaces the conversation history with the summary
axes.permissions:
**A two-level approval design — the finest on this site.**

**Level one is the Plan / Act dual mode.** In Plan mode Cline explores the codebase, asks clarifying questions,
and lays out a strategy; once aligned, switch to Act mode to execute the plan.

**Level two is "every file edit and terminal command needs approval"**, switchable to auto-approve
for autonomous running. The VS Code extension form's wording is **"human-in-the-loop approval"**.

⚠ **But the CLI / headless default is the opposite. This must be known**
(verified against the official CLI Overview and CLI Reference):

- `--auto-approve <boolean>` **defaults to true** — i.e. tools are allowed by default
- with `--auto-approve false`, every tool call needs approval first
- `--yolo` skips all approvals
- **ACP (editor-integration) mode defaults to the opposite**, false

Also: **the CLI has no shell-command allow/deny list**. The official suggests intercepting with a PreToolUse hook.

**CLI prompt original wording**: Default to start in act mode with auto-approve enabled
**VS Code extension wording**: use tools with human-in-the-loop approval
axes.fit:
**Fits four kinds of people:**

- those needing one tool to cover **editor, terminal and desktop** work forms
- those needing **model choice** (not bound to a single vendor)
- those needing **CI/CD integration** (CLI headless)
- those needing a "changes are reviewable and rollbackable" guarantee — diff presentation + wholesale checkpoint undo

sections.权限设计：明确的人工审批:
VS Code extension form, README original wording:

```
use tools with human-in-the-loop approval
```

**This is a rare explicit statement in this category** —
most tools do not state on the README's first screen that tool execution needs human approval.

**The CLI / headless approval stance has been verified** (official CLI Overview and CLI Reference):
the prompt says **"Default to start in act mode with auto-approve enabled"**,
`--auto-approve <boolean>` **defaults to true** — headless runs allow tools by default,
`--auto-approve false` switches to approval before every tool call. `--yolo` skips all approvals.
ACP (editor-integration) mode defaults to the opposite, false.
Also: the CLI has no shell-command allow/deny list. The official suggests intercepting with a PreToolUse hook.

**So "approvals are consistent across the three forms" does not hold**: the extension form requires human approval by default,
the CLI defaults to autonomous allowance — when crossing forms you must align explicitly via `--auto-approve`.
sections.值得单独记的两处设计:
### ① Plan / Act dual mode

In Plan mode it only explores the codebase, asks questions and lays out a strategy — **it does not execute**;
it only acts after switching to Act once aligned. This is the mechanized implementation of "think it through before changing".

### ② Monitoring linter and compiler errors

README original wording:

> It monitors linter and compiler errors as it works, fixing issues like
> missing imports, type mismatches, and syntax errors before you even see them.

**It proactively fixes "type mismatches" and "missing imports"** —
which happens to be the hardest part to judge in this repository's measured task set, and is worth verifying on its own.
